text.text_excerpt: This place is awesome. The decor is funky, the baristas are friendly, and the customers are fresh. This place is def a laid back, chill and enjoy your coffee spot while reading a leisure book or trying to get some serious work done. The barista made me an awesome chai tea latte which was probably better than my mom makes back home or better than the chai tea I can get back in India which was pretty cool. I def dig this place and plan on heading back sooner than later. I suggest you check it out too. The prices are reasonable and the parking is easy on the street and around the corner.

Zotz is one of my favorite places to swing by after a long night at work downtown, a hot summer day, or a cold winter evening. The ambiance is perfect for sitting down with a cup of Earl Grey and enjoying a good book or just casually browsing the internet. Keep in mind that this place is as local as it gets. No overpriced Starbucks mocha grande super expresso dulce caramel pumpkin crappuccino-loso here. You want coffee? Black? You got it. Small, medium, or large? You got it. Soy or regular milk? You got it. Care for a cookie or bagel? You got it. I love this place because they keep it simple, it's open late, and the baristas are super cool. Love Zotz!!

One of my favorite coffeshops in New Orleans! I definitely took advantage of their late operating hours a few years ago when insomnia and I were BFFs. The music is always eclectic (sometimes I'll be in there and the Pogues will be playing and sometimes it'll be Sissy Nobby or Nine Inch Nails) and both baristas and patrons alike are always laid back and amicable. There's a bookshelf in the middle room with a whole lot of random books for your perusal and the wifi (though sometime shaky) is free. Not to mention a shelf with all sorts of old games (Cold War-era Trivial Pursuit, anyone?) to keep you occupied if you happen to find yourself there without a book or a laptop or something to pass ...
